Welcome back, Existing!

Add your API key

Your key is encrypted at rest and only used to generate your personal exercise sets and reviews. Usage is tracked per-user for transparency.

Paste an Anthropic key (console.anthropic.com, starts with sk-ant-), a Google Gemini key (aistudio.google.com, starts with AQ. or the older AIza), or an OpenAI key (platform.openai.com, starts with sk-proj-).

A key replaces the one saved for its provider and switches to it. Keys for other providers stay saved.

Provider in use

Switch between the keys you've saved. To add another provider, paste its key above.

Choose the language your daily exercise sets are generated in. "Mixed" alternates between Ruby/Rails and JavaScript one full day at a time.

Sets when your day rolls over and when your 8am exercise set is generated. Leave on "detect automatically" to use your browser's zone.

Daily sections

Automatic gives you shorter sets after days you don't finish, and longer ones once you finish more and your reviewed answers go well. A number sets how many sections each day is planned with, though a section that fails a quality check can still be left out. 2 gives you only Code Review and Design Comparison.

How hard your sections start out, unless you've set a difficulty for that section in the Exercise mix below. Junior suits early-career developers and career changers. Your ratings still nudge each day's set up or down.

Exercise mix

Bias how often each rotating section appears, and set how hard any section is pitched. Neither changes how many sections a day holds — that's the setting above. Changes save automatically.

Excluding is a stronger, different action than turning a slider down.

A slider at Much less means rarely — the section can still come up, and it will if you haven't seen it in a long while, so nothing disappears from your rotation permanently.

Exclude means never. The section is removed from rotation entirely and will not appear again until you turn it back on.

Excluding also makes the whole group come up less often on shorter days. Fewer kinds left means the ones that remain are seen more often and stay fresh, so the group gives way to groups holding something you haven't seen.

Locking a difficulty target

Lock means this section is always pitched at the level you chose. Easing for concepts you're finding hard, and adjustments from your difficulty ratings, stop applying to it — including the first time you meet a concept. Your progress is still tracked, and unlocking uses it again straight away.
